lina_support: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-inc) hit our /v1/ranking endpoint and is getting weird score ranges. They see a mix of large negative numbers and some tiny positives. They're worried it's a bug because their frontend expects 0..1.

omar_engineering: Thanks Lina. Can you paste a redacted request + request_id? Also which model variant they're hitting?

lina_support: Request id: req_8f3b2a. Model: rwd-ranking-v2 (default). Payload (trimmed):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ranking \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -d '{"query":"best pizza near me","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"..."}, {"id":"c2","text":"..."}], "max_candidates":50 }'
```
Response snippet: 
```
{"scores": [ -2.314, 0.123, -0.87 ], "candidate_ids": ["c1","c2","c3"]}
```
Customer says they expected probabilities (0..1) and billing/threshold logic flagged items incorrectly.

jess_prod: Quick note — we changed the default output to raw logits in v2 to give downstream systems freedom to normalize. We added a flag `normalize_scores` but the client libs didn't default it to true. That might be the root cause.

kevin_repro: Reproduced locally against rwd-ranking-v2. The model returns float logits (can be negative). Applying softmax across candidates transforms those logits into probabilities. Example in Python: 
```python
import numpy as np
logits = np.array([-2.314, 0.123, -0.87])
probs = np.exp(logits) / np.exp(logits).sum()
# -> [0.058, 0.684, 0.258]
```
So negative values are expected — they're not probabilities. They also scale with model head and sequence length.

omar_engineering: Good catch. Also watch out for input formatting that can change logits: if the candidate texts are padded/truncated inconsistently or if you accidentally batch across queries, the relative logits can shift. Are they sending multiple queries in one request or a single query with many candidates?

lina_support: They batch 1 query with ~120 candidates. They set max_candidates client-side to 200 and rely on server to truncate. Could hitting >128 cause any weirdness?

kevin_repro: Two things: 1) We currently clamp internal candidate softmax over the returned slice; if they exceed `max_candidates` it may return a partial slice with no renormalization unless `normalize_scores` is true. 2) Some older client libs did padding with empty strings which the model treats differently, changing logits. Repro steps I ran: send single query with 120 distinct candidates -> raw logits similar magnitude. Then run server-side softmax -> well-formed probabilities.

jess_prod: Actionable items: (a) Support reply should explain that scores are logits by default, not normalized probabilities; (b) give them a one-liner fix: set `normalize_scores: true` in request OR run softmax client-side; (c) warn about batching/ordering/padding; (d) ask for request_id + full payload if they still disagree.

lina_support: Drafting reply to customer saying: "Scores returned by the ranking model are raw logits (can be negative). To get 0..1 probabilities, either set `normalize_scores: true` on the request (recommended) or compute softmax over the `scores` array on your side. Example JS: `const probs = scores.map(s => Math.exp(s)/scores.map(Math.exp).reduce((a,b)=>a+b))`". Also include a small repro snippet and note about `max_candidates` default 100 and that exceeding it may change response shape.

omar_engineering: Also include note: billing is token-based; scores don't affect billing. If they used thresholding on raw logits client-side for feature flags, they'll need to switch to probability thresholds. Add a QR to migration doc.

support-bot: Incident note created: CS-7192, assigned to lina_support. ETA for customer update: 30m.

lina_support: Thanks all. I'll send the explainer + code snippet and ask for the full payload and `req_8f3b2a` logs if they still see mismatch. Will follow up here once they respond. :thumbsup:
